correctness.rationale: For even N, conjugation followed by the checkerboard sign removes the sign change in the time evolution up to endpoint phases. Reflection fixes vertex zero for all N and exchanges the two fluxes. For the odd case, lift two paths to endpoint displacements s,t congruent to j mod N. Their relative phase is exp(i(s−t)φ/N). Only s≠t can contribute to the flux-odd part, and their total length is at least |s−t|≥N. For degree N and 0<j<N the only unordered displacement pair is {j,j−N}, and both paths are monotone. The interference phase from the ordering (j,j−N) is i^(N−2j)exp(iφ), giving the stated sign; including the conjugate term and subtracting the reversed flux produces the factor 4. For winding difference one, total parity is N mod 2, so degree N+1 vanishes; higher winding differences cost at least 2N>N+1. Averaging multiplies degree d by d!/r^d. The uniformly convergent Neumann series for r>4J bounds the remainder starting at N+2 independently of φ. Absolute values preserve that uniform error by the triangle inequality, and the binomial sum gives the stated TV leading term. Independent lifted path counts at φ=π/2 corroborated 627 site-and-degree coefficients for N=3 through 11.
residual_risks: Asymptotic at fixed N and high reset rates; no assertion of nonvanishing for every positive rate or uniformity in N.

The distinct finding is the sharp odd-cycle off-origin coefficient for every vertex and its stationary total-variation law. The strongest checked overlaps do not state or directly supply this calculation for general odd cycles.

value.rationale: It quantifies the first available magnetic-sign signal from stationary position-only readout, identifying its exact attenuation with cycle length and reset rate and the full distributional coefficient. This is more informative than the known qualitative odd chirality and does not claim an even-cycle quantum-state impossibility.
residual_risks: No optimal finite reset rate, transient contrast or full-state discrimination is determined.
